title: adaptive-reconnect-hedging-and-client-abort-window
author: Marina Geller
description:
Motivation: production traffic showed two related failure modes for long-lived streaming sessions: (1) transient host-level stalls cause long tail reconnects that then overwhelm downstream model capacity during bursts, and (2) aggressive client-side aborts lead to lost tool invocations and inconsistent outputs when servers enforce a hard immediate cancel. This PR introduces an adaptive reconnect hedging probe plus a configurable client-abort window with soft-abort semantics to reduce both overloading and spurious tool call duplication while preserving OpenAI-compat streaming semantics.

What this changes: adds a backpressure-aware hedging probe that issues a parallel light reconnect attempt when server-side processing latency crosses a workload-adaptive threshold; introduces a soft-abort window on the server that accepts a short grace period after a client cancel to complete idempotent tool calls and to produce a deterministic final token; surfaces two new API-facing config knobs (stream.reconnect_hedging.enabled, stream.client_abort_window_ms) exposed via the OpenAI-compat adapter with sane defaults and canary gating.

Compatibility and rollouts: default behavior mirrors current semantics (hedging disabled, abort_window_ms=0) until feature-flagged for canary cohort; OpenAI compatibility adapter preserves event ordering and will emit an explicit event type "hedge_probe" on the wire for observability consumers. No breaking changes for existing SDKs.

Testing and validation: unit tests for hedging probe scheduling and probe cancellation; integration flake tests that simulate stall->hedge->failover scenarios; long-running soak test at 10% canary on dedicated infra for 48h. Benchmarks show a 22% reduction in 99.9th percentile session reconnection latency under synthetic stall injections and a ~2% median increase in extraneous probe traffic which is controlled by adaptive thresholds.

Metrics and observability: new metrics: stream.hedge.probes_issued, stream.hedge.probe_success_rate, stream.abort.soft_window_accepts, stream.abort.soft_window_rejects. Added dashboard tile and alert: HedgeProbeFailureRate > 1% for 5m.

Related work: follows design notes in Linear ENG-1871 and references prior server-lease work (ENG-1369) for session fencing. Linked support ticket SUP-8122 for a customer incident that motivated larger abort window experimentation.

Rollout plan: merge to main, with a behind-flag canary (10% traffic -> 50% -> 100%) over two weeks. Monitor hedging probe success rate and tool duplication counters before enabling wider abort window (>250ms).

review_comments: Carlos Mendes (requested changes): Can we make the default abort_window_ms 0 to avoid surprising customers? Also request an explicit note in the docs about idempotency guarantees for tool calls.

Marina Geller (author reply): I changed the default to 0 and added a section in docs/streaming-lifecycle.md outlining idempotency expectations and recommended customer configuration. Also added a feature-flag gating plan to rollout notes.
Aisha Patel (nit): Please add more logging when a hedge probe is cancelled due to successful primary progress; that's useful for our trace correlation dashboards.
Marina Geller (author reply): Added probe_cancel logging with trace_id and probe_latency fields; updated tests to assert logging emitted.
Evan Liu (approved): Verified integration test harness reproduces stall scenario and sees expected hedging behavior. Metrics emitted as described. Approving for merge after CI green.
release_notes: Adds adaptive reconnect hedging probes and a configurable client abort soft-window to reduce spurious reconnect storms and preserve deterministic tool finalization. Backwards-compatible and disabled by default.
